title: Establishing a genetically engineered mouse model of IDH1-mutant astrocytoma
author: Shi, Lee, et al.
materials:
Timing: 1 h
7.Sterilize all surgical tools.a.Place surgical scissors, drill bits, syringe/needles, forceps, stapler, and staples in autoclavable container.b.Use a gravity autoclave setting at 121°C for a minimum of 30 min.c.Remove tools and let cool to room temperature (20°C–23°C).8.Prepare aliquots of sterile PBS.a.Prepare sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes with 1 mL aliquots of sterile PBS inside a laminar flow hood. These will be used for flushing the syringe/needle used for intracranial injection between injections. Prepare at least one aliquoted tube per mouse to be injected.b.Separately, prepare a 50 mL tube of sterile PBS inside a laminar flow hood. This will be used for rinsing surgical tools (scissors, forceps) between mice.9.Prepare aliquots of iodopovidone-based disinfectant.a.Prepare 1 mL aliquots of iodopovidone disinfectant solution (such as Wescodyne®) in sterile Eppendorf tubes. These will also be used to clean the syringe/needle used for intracranial injection between injections. Prepare at least one aliquoted tube per mouse to be injected.b.Separately, prepare a 50 mL tube of iodopovidone disinfectant solution. This will be used for disinfecting surgical tools (scissors, forceps) between mice.10.Aliquot AAV (1 μL per mouse) into a sterile Eppendorf tube. Store AAV on ice throughout surgeries. AAV should be stored as single-use aliquots at −80°C long-term and should not undergo multiple freeze-thaw cycles.
Pause point: Protocol can be paused here for days to weeks before day of surgery.

steps.title: Prepare high‑titer AAV vector
steps.instruction: Propagate the pAAV plasmid pAAV2-sgTrp53-sgAtrx-EFS-Cre (Addgene 189977) and obtain a high‑titer AAV preparation (serotype AAV‑DJ) from a commercial packaging service (e.g., Charles River). Ensure the viral titer is between 1 × 10^13 and 1 × 10^14 genome copies per milliliter; this high titer is required because only ≤3 µL can be injected intracranially.

substeps.instruction: Order or produce AAV‑DJ particles containing the plasmid; verify titer falls within 1 × 10^13–1 × 10^14 gc/mL.

steps.title: Autoclave surgical instruments
steps.instruction: Sterilize all surgical tools (scissors, drill bits, syringes/needles, forceps, stapler, and staples) in an autoclavable container using a gravity autoclave at 121 °C for a minimum of 30 min, then allow them to cool to room temperature (20 °C–23 °C) before use.

substeps.instruction: Place all tools in an autoclavable container.
Run a gravity autoclave cycle at 121 °C for ≥30 min.
Remove tools and let cool to 20 °C–23 °C.

steps.title: Aliquot sterile PBS for injections
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow hood, prepare sterile PBS aliquots: dispense 1 mL sterile PBS into each 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube (one tube per mouse) for flushing the injection syringe/needle, and also prepare a single 50 mL tube of sterile PBS for rinsing surgical tools between mice.

substeps.instruction: Label 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and add 1 mL sterile PBS to each (≥1 tube per mouse).
Label a 50 mL tube and fill with sterile PBS for tool rinsing.

steps.title: Aliquot iodopovidone disinfectant
steps.instruction: Prepare iodopovidone‑based disinfectant (e.g., Wescodyne®) aliquots: dispense 1 mL into sterile Eppendorf tubes (one per mouse) for cleaning the injection syringe/needle, and also prepare a 50 mL tube of the same solution for disinfecting surgical tools between mice.

substeps.instruction: Label 1 mL Eppendorf tubes and add 1 mL iodopovidone disinfectant to each (≥1 tube per mouse).
Label a 50 mL tube and fill with iodopovidone disinfectant for tool disinfection.

steps.title: Aliquot AAV for each mouse
steps.instruction: Aliquot 1 µL of the high‑titer AAV preparation into a sterile Eppendorf tube for each mouse; keep the aliquoted virus on ice during the surgeries. Store long‑term as single‑use aliquots at –80 °C and avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles.
